title: Soil Mechanics: Numerical Practice Set 1 (Moderate to Hard)
instructions: All 40 questions are numerical, of moderate to hard level. Keep rough paper ready.
Take the unit weight of water as 10 kN/m³ where the question says so, and use the factors given in each question.

questions.question: A fully saturated soil has a water content of 20% and a specific gravity of solids of 2.7. Its void ratio is:
A soil has a bulk unit weight of 18 kN/m³ and a water content of 20%. Its dry unit weight is:
A soil has a void ratio of 0.6. Its porosity is:
A soil has a specific gravity of solids of 2.65 and a void ratio of 0.65. Taking γ_w = 10 kN/m³, its saturated unit weight is:
A soil has a bulk unit weight of 18 kN/m³, a water content of 15% and a specific gravity of solids of 2.7. Taking γ_w = 10 kN/m³, its degree of saturation is approximately:
A sand has maximum and minimum void ratios of 0.9 and 0.5. Its void ratio in the field is 0.6. Its relative density is:
A clay has a liquid limit of 50%, a plastic limit of 25% and a natural water content of 35%. Its liquidity index is:
questions.explanation: LI = (w − PL) / (LL − PL) = (35 − 25) / (50 − 25) = 0.4. (The consistency index is 0.6.)

questions.question: The A-line of the plasticity chart is PI = 0.73 (LL − 20). For a soil with a liquid limit of 50%, the plasticity index on the A-line is:
From a grain size curve, D₁₀ = 0.15 mm, D₃₀ = 0.30 mm and D₆₀ = 0.60 mm. The coefficient of curvature is:
questions.explanation: C_c = D₃₀² / (D₆₀ × D₁₀) = 0.30² / (0.60 × 0.15) = 1.0. (The uniformity coefficient is D₆₀/D₁₀ = 4.0.)

questions.question: A soil has a plasticity index of 30% and 40% of its particles are finer than 2 microns. Its activity is:
In a constant head permeability test, 600 cm³ of water passes in 60 s through a sample 15 cm long and 50 cm² in cross-section, under a constant head of 30 cm. The coefficient of permeability is:
In a falling head test, the sample is 10 cm long and 50 cm² in area, and the standpipe area is 1 cm². The head falls from 100 cm to 50 cm in 300 s. The coefficient of permeability is approximately:
Water flows through a soil with k = 3 × 10⁻³ cm/s under a hydraulic gradient of 0.5. The void ratio of the soil is 0.6. The seepage velocity is:
questions.explanation: Discharge velocity v = ki = 3 × 10⁻³ × 0.5 = 1.5 × 10⁻³ cm/s. Porosity n = 0.6 / 1.6 = 0.375. Seepage velocity = v / n = 4.0 × 10⁻³ cm/s.

questions.question: A deposit has two horizontal layers: the upper is 2 m thick with k = 4 × 10⁻⁴ cm/s and the lower is 3 m thick with k = 1 × 10⁻⁴ cm/s. The equivalent permeability for vertical flow is approximately:
questions.explanation: k_v = ΣH / Σ(H/k) = (2 + 3) / (2/4 + 3/1) = 5 / 3.5 ≈ 1.43 × 10⁻⁴ cm/s. (For horizontal flow it is 2.20 × 10⁻⁴ cm/s.)

questions.question: A flow net under a dam has 4 flow channels and 12 equipotential drops. The head lost is 6 m and k = 1 × 10⁻⁵ m/s. The seepage per metre length of the dam is approximately:
A sand has a specific gravity of solids of 2.7 and a void ratio of 0.8. The critical hydraulic gradient for a quick condition is approximately:

The water table is 2 m below ground level. The soil above it has a unit weight of 17 kN/m³ and the soil below has a saturated unit weight of 20 kN/m³. Taking γ_w = 10 kN/m³, the effective vertical stress at a depth of 6 m is:
questions.explanation: Total stress = 17 × 2 + 20 × 4 = 114 kPa. Pore pressure = 10 × 4 = 40 kPa. Effective stress = 114 − 40 = 74 kPa.

questions.question: A soil has a unit weight of 18 kN/m³ above the water table and a saturated unit weight of 20 kN/m³. The water table rises from a depth of 5 m to the ground surface. Taking γ_w = 10 kN/m³, the decrease in effective stress at a depth of 5 m is:
questions.explanation: Before: σ′ = 18 × 5 = 90 kPa. After: σ′ = (20 − 10) × 5 = 50 kPa. Decrease = 40 kPa.

questions.question: Water seeps vertically upwards through a saturated soil (γ_sat = 20 kN/m³) under a hydraulic gradient of 0.3. Taking γ_w = 10 kN/m³, the effective stress at a depth of 4 m below the soil surface is:
A point load of 1000 kN acts on the ground surface. By Boussinesq's equation, the vertical stress at a depth of 2 m directly below the load is approximately:
A compacted fill has a bulk unit weight of 19.5 kN/m³ at a water content of 14%. The maximum dry unit weight from the Proctor test is 18.0 kN/m³. The relative compaction is approximately:
A soil has a specific gravity of solids of 2.7. Taking γ_w = 10 kN/m³, the dry unit weight on the zero air voids line at a water content of 15% is approximately:

A normally consolidated clay layer 4 m thick has C_c = 0.3 and an initial void ratio of 1.0. The effective stress at its centre increases from 100 kPa to 200 kPa. The consolidation settlement is approximately:
A clay layer 3 m thick has a coefficient of volume compressibility of 5 × 10⁻⁴ m²/kN. The effective stress increases by 60 kPa. The consolidation settlement is:

A laboratory clay sample 20 mm thick, drained on both faces, reaches 50% consolidation in 10 minutes. A layer of the same clay 4 m thick, also drained on both faces, will reach 50% consolidation in approximately:
questions.explanation: Time is proportional to the square of the drainage path: t = 10 × (4000 / 20)² = 400000 minutes = 400000 / 1440 ≈ 277.78 days.

questions.question: A clay layer 4 m thick is drained at the top only and has c_v = 2 m²/year. Using T_v = (π/4)U², the time for 50% consolidation is approximately:
questions.explanation: T_v = (π/4) × 0.5² = 0.196. Drainage path d = 4 m (single drainage). t = T_v d² / c_v = 0.196 × 16 / 2 ≈ 1.57 years.

questions.question: In a consolidation test, the void ratio falls from 0.90 to 0.78 when the effective stress rises from 100 kPa to 200 kPa. The compression index is approximately:
A soil has c = 20 kPa and φ = 30°. The shear strength on a plane where the effective normal stress is 100 kPa is approximately:
A soil with c = 20 kPa and φ = 30° is tested in a triaxial cell at a confining pressure of 100 kPa. The major principal stress at failure is approximately:
In a drained triaxial test on a clean sand (c = 0), the cell pressure is 150 kPa and the deviator stress at failure is 300 kPa. The angle of shearing resistance is:
A smooth vertical wall 6 m high retains dry cohesionless backfill with γ = 18 kN/m³ and φ = 30°. By Rankine's theory, the total active thrust per metre length of wall is:
A smooth vertical wall 3 m high is pushed against dry cohesionless soil with γ = 18 kN/m³ and φ = 30°. By Rankine's theory, the total passive resistance per metre length is:
questions.explanation: K_p = (1 + sin 30°) / (1 − sin 30°) = 3. P_p = ½ K_p γ H² = ½ × 3 × 18 × 9 = 243 kN per metre.

questions.question: A wall retains a soil with c = 20 kPa, φ = 20° and γ = 18 kN/m³. In the active state, the depth of the tension crack is approximately:
A smooth vertical wall 5 m high retains dry sand (γ = 18 kN/m³, φ = 30°) carrying a uniform surcharge of 20 kPa. The total active thrust per metre length is approximately:
questions.explanation: K_a = 1/3. Soil: ½ × (1/3) × 18 × 25 = 75 kN. Surcharge: K_a q H = (1/3) × 20 × 5 = 33.33 kN. Total = 108.33 kN per metre.

questions.question: A smooth vertical wall 4 m high retains sand that is saturated up to the top, with γ_sat = 20 kN/m³ and φ = 30°. Taking γ_w = 10 kN/m³, the total lateral thrust (soil plus water) per metre length is approximately:
questions.explanation: Soil (submerged weight): ½ × (1/3) × (20 − 10) × 16 = 26.67 kN. Water: ½ × 10 × 16 = 80 kN. Total = 106.67 kN per metre.

questions.question: A strip footing 2 m wide is founded 1.5 m deep in sand with c = 0 and γ = 18 kN/m³. The bearing capacity factors are N_q = 22.5 and N_γ = 19.7. By Terzaghi's equation, the ultimate bearing capacity is:
A strip footing is founded 1 m deep in a saturated clay with c_u = 50 kPa, φ_u = 0 and γ = 18 kN/m³. Using Terzaghi's N_c = 5.7 and a factor of safety of 3, the net safe bearing capacity is:
questions.explanation: For φ = 0, N_q = 1 and N_γ = 0, so the net ultimate bearing capacity = c N_c = 5.7 × 50 = 285 kPa. Net safe bearing capacity = 285 / 3 = 95 kPa.

questions.question: A square footing 2 m × 2 m is founded 1 m deep in a soil with c = 10 kPa and γ = 18 kN/m³. The bearing capacity factors are N_c = 37.2, N_q = 22.5 and N_γ = 19.7. By Terzaghi's equation for a square footing, the ultimate bearing capacity is approximately:
A bored pile 0.4 m in diameter and 10 m long is installed in clay with c_u = 50 kPa. Taking N_c = 9 at the base and an adhesion factor of 0.6, its ultimate load capacity is approximately:

In a plate load test on sand, a 0.3 m plate settles 10 mm under the design pressure. Using S_f = S_p [B_f (B_p + 0.3) / (B_p (B_f + 0.3))]², the settlement of a footing 1.5 m wide under the same pressure is approximately:
